title: Minimum Insertions to Balance a Parentheses String
summary: Given a string s with parentheses '(', ')', a string is balanced if every '(' has a corresponding '))' and '(' precedes '))'.
statement: Given a string s with parentheses '(', ')', a string is balanced if every '(' has a corresponding '))' and '(' precedes '))'. You can insert '(' and ')' to balance the string. Return the minimum insertions needed to achieve a balanced string.
constraints: Every opening parenthesis must be matched by two consecutive closing parentheses.
Insert the fewest parentheses anywhere to make s balanced.
hints: Track how many closing parentheses are currently required.
Before a new opening, if the requirement is odd, insert one closing parenthesis so previous pairs stay consecutive.
A closing consumes one requirement; if it makes need negative, insert an opening and leave one closing still required.
Each repair is forced at the position where the grammar would otherwise become impossible, so the greedy count is minimal.
editorial: Each repair is forced at the position where the grammar would otherwise become impossible, so the greedy count is minimal.

tests.explanation: The first opening is closed by the final pair, while one closing parenthesis must be inserted for the other opening.
One opening followed by two closings is already balanced, so no insertion is needed.
